data.cultural_impact: The name Sarvani holds great significance in Indian culture as it reflects the belief in the interconnectedness of all things and the idea of inclusivity and oneness. It is a name that symbolizes unity and harmony among all beings. Sarvani is also a popular name for Goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge, arts, and wisdom, reflecting her all-encompassing nature and power.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Sarvani represents the concept of Brahman, the ultimate reality and the source of all creation, which is omnipresent and everywhere. It signifies the idea that everything in the universe is an expression of the divine and that we are all connected to the Source. Sarvani highlights the importance of recognizing the divine spark within each one of us and treating all beings with love, compassion, and respect.

historical_references.reference: Sarvani was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, which ruled large parts of ancient India from the 3rd century BCE to the 3rd century CE. She is best known for her association with the Satavahana king Rudradaman I, with whom she is believed to have ruled jointly.

Another reference mentions Sarvani as a queen of the Vakataka dynasty, which emerged in the 3rd century CE in the Deccan region of India. She is known for her patronage of the Buddhist monk Haritabhadra and her role in the spread of Buddhism in the region.
